stem: A client has marked proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, generalized edema, and hyperlipidemia. Which renal syndrome is most consistent with this pattern?
rationale: NCBI StatPearls defines nephrotic syndrome by substantial proteinuria causing hypoalbuminemia, with resulting edema and hyperlipidemia due to abnormal glomerular permeability. Therefore A matches the complete pattern. B is more strongly associated with glomerular inflammation, hematuria, hypertension, and impaired renal function, although some proteinuria may occur. C is caused by reduced renal perfusion and does not produce this characteristic glomerular protein-loss pattern. D results from urinary outflow obstruction and likewise does not explain the combination of marked proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia.
educational_objective: Differentiate nephrotic syndrome by its characteristic pattern of heavy protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia from nephritic and hemodynamic/obstructive kidney disorders.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine — NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Nephrotic Syndrome — StatPearls; Acute Kidney Injury — StatPearls
source_version_date: Nephrotic Syndrome last updated 2023-05-29; current NCBI pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Nephrotic Syndrome > Continuing Education Activity/Introduction: massive proteinuria responsible for hypoalbuminemia with resulting hyperlipidemia and edema, caused by abnormal glomerular permeability. Nephrotic Syndrome > History and Physical: edema is prominent; hematuria and hypertension are more prominent in nephritic syndrome. Acute Kidney Injury > Etiology: prerenal AKI reflects reduced renal blood flow and postrenal AKI obstructive causes.
source_claim_supported: Marked proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia is the characteristic nephrotic-syndrome pattern and differs from nephritic, prerenal, and postrenal processes.
